bugs.text: The player can never fire. G.fireCd is never initialised, so 'G.fireCd<=0' is undefined<=0 (false) and line 601 cannot set it either. No shot is ever created; the only way to score is ramming, no stage can be cleared, and every feature behind a bullet hit (boss two-hit colour change, rescue, dual fighter, captive destruction, stage advance, challenge stages, extra ships) is unreachable. Play-test: NUMBER OF SHOTS 0 after two games, no player bullets in any screenshot.

A Boss Galaga that holds a captured fighter is excluded from the dive pool (`!(e.type==='boss'&&e.captured)` and `!k.captured`), so it never dives again. The rescue (398, 541-551), the dual fighter (547) and the captive firing at the player (535-537) can therefore never happen even if shooting worked; a captured ship is simply lost.

updateChal is defined but never called, so a challenging stage spawns nothing; beginStage also leaves G.stageT from the previous stage, so the empty 'play' state is treated as cleared after 1.6 s and the game jumps to the next stage. No fly-through waves, no NUMBER OF HITS screen, no bonus.
sHit (enemy-hit sound) is defined but never called; a non-fatal hit on a boss uses sBossHit only, and no other 'hit' sound exists.

G.hits is incremented twice for a bullet kill in a challenge stage (once in updateCollisions, once in killEnemy), so the hit-miss ratio could exceed 100% (unreachable at present because of the firing and updateChal bugs).

Every enemy in formation fires bullets aimed straight at the player (tryFire in the 'formation' state), about 3-4 aimed shots per second once the formation is full. The arcade only fires from divers; here a still player dies within seconds (the play-test lost three ships in about 10 s).
hitPlayer returns while invulnerable but killEnemy runs first, so during the 1 s blink after a respawn the player can ram enemies for full points with no cost.
The beam dive targets the player's x and the catch zone is about 88 px wide at the player's row (half the screen), so almost any boss beam dive captures a player who does not move far.
All stage badges are drawn identically; the 1/5/10/20/30/50 denominations are only counted, not shown.
Formation sway never stops after the formation is complete, breathing only stretches rows vertically, and the per-row sway factor shears the formation sideways.
Title screen prints 'C O N G R A T U L A T I O N S !' above the score table and spells Goei as 'GOEIE'.
Escort selection compares the boss column (4-wide grid) with goei columns (8-wide grid) directly, so escorts are often not the goei under the boss.

summary: The file is tidy and well organised: a proper fixed-timestep loop, a clean state/update/render split, data-defined pixel sprites with wing flap, generated explosion frames, bezier entry and dive paths, an animated tractor beam, synthesized Web Audio, and a HUD, title, results and stage flow that all look like Galaga in the screenshots. But one missing initialiser (G.fireCd) means the player can never fire a shot, so the game cannot be played as Galaga at all: nothing can be destroyed except by ramming, no stage can be cleared, and the boss two-hit, rescue, dual fighter, challenge stage and extra-ship rules are all dead code. Two further logic bugs would survive a fix of that one: a boss that holds a captive is barred from diving, which kills the signature rescue mechanic, and updateChal is never called, so challenging stages are empty and skipped. The formation also fires aimed shots from every slot, which is far more hostile than the arcade. Visually faithful, mechanically broken.
